findings.location: ## Definition, paragraph beginning ‘In the common natural-unit field convention’
findings.evidence: The item assigns dimensions to scalar and Dirac fields without defining their maps/types or stating the four-dimensional kinetic-action normalization that fixes these canonical dimensions. Tong §0.1 supplies natural units and mass dimensions generally, but not these field-dimension hypotheses ([Tong, §0.1](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/qft/qfthtml/S0.html), lines 64–83). The assertion needs exact field types and normalization conditions or an authoritative source stating them.

findings.location: ## Definition, gauge-notation paragraph defining A_lower, D_a, A -> A+dχ, and ψ -> exp(iqχ/ħ)ψ
findings.evidence: The gauge symbols are not defined as maps on a specified spacetime domain; the types of A, χ, and ψ and the regularity required for ∂_a are omitted. Tong §1.1 describes fields as quantities defined at every point of space and time and identifies spatial/vector types for electromagnetic fields ([Tong, §1.1](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/qft/qfthtml/S1.html), lines 26–35); the assigned definition gives no corresponding domains/types. The convention needs explicit spacetime/coordinate domains, field types, and regularity.

findings.location: ## Definition and ## Facts & Assumptions, SI constants; ## Proof steps 1.1 and 2.1
findings.evidence: The Given clause says the constants have SI dimensions ‘as stated above,’ but μ0 has no stated unit. Proof 1.1 uses [μ0] = kg m C^-2 to show g dimensionless, and Proof 2.1 uses SI electromagnetic units. BIPM identifies μ0's unit as H m^-1 (equivalently kg m C^-2) ([BIPM, SI Brochure, 9th ed., Table 4 and Appendix 1, Resolution 1](https://www.bipm.org/utils/common/pdf/si-brochure/SI-Brochure-9.pdf), printed pp. 134 and 189, PDF pp. 135 and 190); the premise must be stated or linked exactly.

The stated Schwartz test class is complex-valued. For complex φ, ∫xψ/(x²+ε²) is not the real part of the scalar regularized integral, and -∫φε/(x²+ε²) is not its imaginary part. For φ(x)=i exp(-x²), the actual regularized integral has positive real part and zero imaginary part, contrary to these identifications. The Plemelj conclusion can be true, but the proof's displayed real/imaginary-part calculations are false as written; decompose the kernel contributions with the required factor -i or prove real and imaginary test components separately.

findings.location: ## Statement, distributional derivative and Fourier-limit clauses; ## Proof, steps 3.1–3.2 and 4.1
findings.evidence: The item uses distributional derivatives and a distributional Fourier limit without stating the distribution/derivative convention, declaring a supplier for it, or specifying the limit topology. Its dependencies do not include these definitions. The published def-distributional-derivative supplies the missing test-function action, while def-tempered-distribution supplies the Schwartz-dual setting used by step 4.1; the item must declare these prerequisites or define the operations and convergence mode locally.

findings.location: Final body paragraph, sentence ‘The local arguments prove every mathematical claim’
findings.evidence: The current oscillator lemma's Plemelj proof contains false real/imaginary-part calculations for its declared complex Schwartz test functions. The page summary therefore asserts proof completion beyond the current item evidence.
